scope: Proposition 8.2 (Inverse estimate for an edge) of the manuscript “A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function” (preprints/A-quadratic-bound-for-Jacobsthals-function-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 021 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f80267eebc82a9b8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 44. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the parameters in (8.3)–(8.5), the witnessing threshold δ > 0, and 0 < σ < 1. There are constants cp > 0, a list-size bound F < ∞, and ξinv > 0, independent of the eventual choice of fixed 0 < ξ ≤ ξinv, with the following property for all sufficiently large z. The full candidate box has a list A of at most F reduced rationals A/D satisfying D ≤ RZ10 , |A| ≤ SqRZ10 , #{p ∈ P : p aligns with A/D} ≥ cpnp. (8.7) Outside a set of normalized harmonic box measure at most σ, every occurrence of Npqu − Npq u > δ Y V0 pqu (8.8) has a rational A/D ∈ A for which p aligns with A/D, DqE(A/D) ≤ RZ10 . (8.9) The exceptional measure is relative to the whole box, rather than to the subset on which (8.8) holds.
